stem: A resident pharmacy is preparing to close. Which timing and transfer statements are supported by 247 CMR 6.13 and 6.14? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Given the described event, delay every patient-file transfer until after all controlled stock has been disposed of.
For this scenario, send the Board's required certified written notice at least 14 days before the intended closure date.
Under these facts, identify patients served during the preceding 90 days and attempt patient notice at least 14 days before closure.
In this setting, handle requested patient-file transfers timely so the closure does not delay therapy.
At this stage, within 14 days after closure, submit original credentials and the controlled-substance disposition attestation.

choice_analysis.C: 'Under these facts, identify patients served during the preceding 90 days and attempt patient notice at least 14 days before closure.': Closure notice supports this proposition.
choice_analysis.D: 'In this setting, handle requested patient-file transfers timely so the closure does not delay therapy.': Closure notice supports this proposition.
choice_analysis.E: 'At this stage, within 14 days after closure, submit original credentials and the controlled-substance disposition attestation.': Closure notice supports this proposition.

related_facts: A resident pharmacy generally must give the Board written certified-mail notice at least 14 days before intended closure and provide the required closure and controlled-substance information.
A closing pharmacy identifies patients served in the preceding 90 days, attempts notice at least 14 days before closure, posts conspicuous notice, and supports timely patient-file transfer.
